To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of rigid fillers to a PP matrix leads to an increase in the fracture toughness.
the presence of particles in PP-based composites strongly affects the values of fracture toughness, which can be increased by a factor 3 or more.
PP composites with nanometric particles show a significant improvement in the fracture toughness, compared to the same materials prepared with microsized particles.

the fracture behaviour of polypropylene (P) based particulate composites.
the fracture toughness of PP composites reinforced by rigid particles, in particular, with the effect of the size of the filler on the values of fracture toughness.

the fracture behaviour of polypropylene-based composites reinforced with rigid particles of different shape, chemical nature, and surface treatment, and the influence of particle size on the fracture toughness of the composites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fracture toughness values are strongly dependent on the particle scale size and concentration, and on the matrix properties, but not on the chemical nature of the particles.

PP-based composites with micrometric particles show a fracture behaviour strongly affected by the particle size and concentration by volume, while for the PP composites containing nanometric fillers, the fracture resistance increases by the increase of the filler content.

the addition of particles in the PP matrix is able to increase the fracture toughness, but the increase is not proportional to the particle volume fraction, but depends on the particle size, shape and orientation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fracture toughness is strongly influenced by the particle scale size, the particle shape and the particle concentration by volume.
the fracture toughness values are strongly influenced by the particles nature, size and orientation, as well as the particle/matrix interfacial adhesion.
the fracture behaviour of polymeric materials is strongly affected by particle addition, but the influence depends on many factors, which are not easy to predict and to control.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the fracture toughness of PP-based composites is strongly dependent on the size and shape of particles and their surface nature, and it is also affected by the orientation and dispersion of particles in the matrix.
the addition of particles to PP matrix is able to increase fracture resistance by the presence of a tortuous crack path, which is more effective in micrometric particles than in nanoparticles.
the fracture toughness is a complex parameter that is strongly dependent on the experimental conditions.
